title: ALMA Detection of the Vibrationally Excited HCN J = 4-3 Emission Line in the AGN-hosting Luminous Infrared Galaxy IRAS 20551-4250
question: Is vibrationally excited HCN J=4-3 emission present in the AGN-hosting LIRG IRAS 20551-4250, and how does its HCN-to-HCO+ J=4-3 flux ratio compare with starburst galaxies?

what.value: IRAS FSC fluxes at 12, 25, 60, 100 um for IR luminosities

evidence.quote: are *IRAS* fluxes at 12 $\mu$m, 25 $\mu$m, 60 $\mu$m, and 100 $\mu$m, respectively, taken from the IRAS *FSC* catalog.

what.value: NGC 1614 HCN/HCO+ and HCN/HNC J=4-3 ratios for comparison

evidence.quote: The ratios at four different positions in the starburst galaxy NGC 1614, taken with our ALMA Cycle 0 observations (cite: ima13), are overplotted for comparison.

what.value: HCN v2=1 to v=0 ratio in NGC 4418

evidence.loc: 4.1 Vibrationally excited HCN J=4–3 emission line
evidence.quote: which is a factor of $\sim$5 smaller than the ratio observed in NGC 4418 (cite: sak10).

recipe.method: Subtract continuum from line-free channels, then clean with 40-channel binning and 0.1" pixels

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and moment maps and fit Gaussians
recipe.method: Moment 0 maps by combining channels with signal; Gaussian fits to spectra at continuum peak within beam
Use eq. (1) of Nakanishi et al. 2005 with far-infrared luminosity, assuming it is all starburst
assumptions: Far-infrared luminosity entirely starburst (upper limit on free-free)

recipe.method: HCN/HCO+ and HCN/HNC J=4-3 flux ratios compared with NGC 1614; vib/v=0 HCN ratio compared with NGC 4418

evidence.loc: 4.1 Vibrationally excited HCN J=4–3 emission line

answer_key.quantity: HCN v2=1 to v=0 flux ratio

evidence.loc: 4.1 Vibrationally excited HCN J=4–3 emission line
evidence.quote: The HCN J=4–3 v$_{2}$=1 (l=1f) to v=0 flux ratio is $\sim$0.04
The HCN-to-HCO$^{+}$ J=4–3 flux ratio ($\sim$0.7) is higher than in the other starburst-dominated galaxy ($\sim$0.2)
